Purpose

Fix LMCache crash when used with MLA (Multi-Latent Attention) models that store KV cache as multiple groups with different dtypes.

Fixes: #2774, #2881

Problem

MLA models like GLM-5-FP8 and DeepSeek V3 store KV cache as two separate groups:

  • Group 0: K_rope — 78 layers, uint8 (FP8), head_dim=132
  • Group 1: Latent KV — 78 layers, bfloat16, head_dim=576

LMCache's kv_layer_groups correctly discovers these groups:

KV layer groups: [
  KVLayerGroupInfo(layers=78, indices=0-77,   shape=[4734, 64, 132],  dtype=uint8),
  KVLayerGroupInfo(layers=78, indices=78-155, shape=[4734, 64, 576],  dtype=bfloat16)
]

But three code paths crash because they assume a single KV group:

Crash 1: memory_management.py — .tensor property reshape

RuntimeError: shape '[1, 78, 256, 132]' is invalid for input of size 25638912

meta.shape only describes Group 0, but raw_data contains both groups concatenated.

Crash 2: gpu_connectors.py — _initialize_pointers broadcast

ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (156,) into shape (78,)

kv_cache_pointers pre-allocated for 78 layers but kv_caches has 156 entries.

Crash 3: gpu_connectors.py — from_gpu tensor size mismatch

RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (25638912) must match the size of tensor b (576)

multi_layer_kv_transfer receives the full flat buffer instead of per-group shaped tensors.

Solution

Five targeted fixes, all backward-compatible (single-group models follow unchanged paths):

  1. memory_management.py: When meta.shapes has >1 entry, .tensor raises ValueError forcing callers to use get_tensor(index) for per-group access.

  2. gpu_connectors.py _initialize_pointers: Detects when kv_caches length exceeds pre-allocated pointer buffer and reallocates. Does NOT mutate self.num_layers (preserves transformer layer count).

  3. gpu_connectors.py from_gpu / to_gpu: When MLA multi-group is detected, iterates over groups, extracts per-group tensors via get_tensor(), builds cached per-group pointers (_get_group_pointers), discovers per-group format, and calls multi_layer_kv_transfer separately per group with correct head_size.

  4. cache_engine.py: Non-first-rank lookup returns total requested tokens when save_only_first_rank is enabled, so min() aggregation in the lookup client defers to rank 0's actual result.

  5. local_disk_backend.py: Preserves multi-group shapes/dtypes through disk round-trip. Allocates with all group shapes on load when multi-group is detected.

Production Validation

Validated on two MLA models in production and staging environments:

GLM-5-FP8 (2 KV groups, v_head_dim=256) — Production H200

  • 8x NVIDIA H200, TP=8, vLLM v0.19.0
  • 3-tier cache: GPU (254K tokens) → CPU (200GB) → NVMe RAID-0 (1.75TB)
  • 1.15M external cache hit tokens under real traffic
  • 500-request XL stress test (50K-180K tokens): 500/500 pass, 0 gibberish
  • 150K prompt reload: 3.3s (cached) vs 27.6s (recompute) — 8.4x speedup

Kimi K2.5 (1 KV group, v_head_dim=128) — Nebius H200

  • 8x NVIDIA H200, TP=8, vLLM v0.19.0
  • 3-tier cache: GPU → CPU (150GB) → Disk (200GB)
  • 810K external cache hit tokens in stress test
  • 145-request XL stress test (74K-222K tokens): 145/145 pass, 0 gibberish, 0 errors
  • All 5 anchors loaded from CPU and disk tiers after eviction (verified via adapter logs)
  • Tool call regression suite: 14/14 pass (kimi_k2 parser)

Deployment note: PYTHONHASHSEED=0

When deploying LMCache with save_only_first_rank=True (default for TP>1), you must set PYTHONHASHSEED=0 as an environment variable. Without it, Python's randomized hash seed differs across the EngineCore scheduler process and TP worker processes, causing lookup hash keys to never match store hash keys — resulting in 0% external cache hit rate with no error messages.

Test Plan

  • New unit tests in tests/v1/test_mla_multi_group.py (7 tests)
    • .tensor raises ValueError for multi-group (prevents misuse)
    • .tensor returns shaped tensor for single-group (backward compat)
    • get_tensor(index) returns correct per-group shape and dtype
    • Raw buffer size equals sum of all groups
    • Per-group views reference non-overlapping memory
    • Non-first-rank lookup returns total tokens (save_only_first_rank fix)
  • Full existing test suite: 328 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (unrelated CLI test), 64 skipped
  • End-to-end: GLM-5-FP8 on 8xH200, production traffic — 1.15M external hits
  • End-to-end: Kimi K2.5 on 8xH200, 3-tier stress test — 810K external hits
  • Tool call compliance: identical results with/without LMCache

Environment Tested

  • vLLM v0.19.0 (vllm/vllm-openai:latest-cu130)
  • LMCache v0.4.2 (vanilla image) + bind-mounted patches from this PR branch
  • LMCache built from source (production GLM-5 image)
  • Models: zai-org/GLM-5-FP8 (78 layers, 2 KV groups), moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5 (61 layers, 1 KV group)
  • GPU: 8x NVIDIA H200 (140GB)
  • CUDA 13.0, Driver 580.126.09
  • LMCache config: local_cpu: true, local_disk: /mnt/lmcache, chunk_size: 256

Note

Medium Risk
Touches GPU KV transfer, memory object semantics, and storage backends (CPU/disk) with new error-handling paths; failures could surface as cache misses or performance regressions, but changes are scoped and backed by extensive regression tests.

Overview
Fixes crashes and data corruption when caching MLA (multi-group) KV layouts (e.g., GLM-5/DeepSeek V3) by treating KV as per-group tensors end-to-end rather than a single shape.

Key changes: GPU connector now resizes pointer buffers for multi-group KV, caches per-group GPU pointer tensors, and runs multi_layer_kv_transfer per group in both directions; MemoryObj.tensor now rejects multi-group access to force get_tensor() usage; disk backend persists multi-group shapes/dtypes for correct allocation on load and correct size accounting, and cleans up leftover .pt files on startup; cache_engine.store() and disk async prefetch add failure cleanup to unpin/release objects to avoid deadlocks; CPU backend adds LazyMemoryAllocator, proportional eviction, and a retry cap to avoid worker stalls; lookup returns total tokens on non-first ranks when save_only_first_rank is enabled.

Adds targeted regression/property tests covering multi-group tensor access, proportional eviction/max-attempts guards, pin-leak cleanup on failures, disk accounting/startup recovery, and allocator churn behavior.

Code Review

This pull request implements support for Multi-Latent Attention (MLA) multi-group KV caches by modifying pointer initialization, the from_gpu transfer logic, and the MemoryObj.tensor property. Review feedback highlights that updating self.num_layers to the total cache count is architecturally incorrect and will cause downstream errors in shape calculation. Bug Report: CPU memory exhaustion causes pin deadlock → vLLM hang

We discovered a production-crashing bug while running this PR's patches on zai-org/GLM-5-FP8 (8x H200, vLLM v0.19.0, LMCache v0.4.2). The server became unresponsive after ~3 hours under real traffic.

Root Cause

When LMCache's CPU memory tier (200 GB) is exhausted, the batched_async_prefetch method in local_disk_backend.py pins disk cache entries but fails to unpin them when the subsequent CPU staging allocation fails. This creates a deadlock:

  1. Disk entries are pinned (line 468: self.dict[key].pin())
  2. CPU staging allocation fails (allocate() returns None)
  3. Method returns partial results — but the already-pinned disk entries from prior loop iterations are never unpinned
  4. Pinned objects hold CPU memory references that can never be freed
  5. The CPU pool is permanently exhausted, and the pin monitor's 300s timeout is the only escape
  6. After force-unpin, the vLLM engine core does not recover — server hangs indefinitely

Similarly, the store() method in cache_engine.py lacks error handling around the from_gpu → batched_put sequence. If either fails, allocated memory_objs are never released.

Timeline from Production Incident

02:01:49  Normal operation — storing 256 tokens, 0.015 GB, 6.1 GB/s throughput
02:02:00  CPU exhaustion — "Failed to allocate memory block of size 15734784" × 3000+
02:02:00  651 GPU memory objects pinned, transfers can't complete
02:02:00–02:22:32  DEADLOCK — vLLM scheduler blocked, no requests served
02:22:32  Pin monitor force-unpins 651 objects after 304.72s timeout
02:22:32+ Server does not recover — health check returns 000, container is zombie

Fix (two changes)

1. local_disk_backend.py — batched_async_prefetch

Track pinned disk keys and unpin them all on allocation failure:

pinned_disk_keys: list[CacheEngineKey] = []

for key in keys:
    # ... existing code ...
    
    memory_obj = self.local_cpu_backend.allocate(shape, dtype, fmt, busy_loop=False)
    
    if memory_obj is None:
        logger.error(
            "Memory allocation failed during async disk load for key %s. "
            "CPU staging pool may be exhausted. Unpinning %d previously "
            "pinned disk keys and returning partial results.",
            key, len(pinned_disk_keys),
        )
        # Unpin all disk entries pinned in this batch to prevent deadlock
        for pinned_key in pinned_disk_keys:
            if pinned_key in self.dict:
                self.dict[pinned_key].unpin()
        for mo in mem_objs:
            if mo.is_pinned:
                mo.unpin()
        self.disk_lock.release()
        return []
    
    self.dict[key].pin()
    pinned_disk_keys.append(key)  # track for cleanup
    # ... rest of loop ...

2. cache_engine.py — store()

Wrap from_gpu + batched_put in try/except to release memory objects on failure:

try:
    with store_stats.profile_from_gpu():
        self.gpu_connector.batched_from_gpu(memory_objs, starts, ends, **kwargs)
    with store_stats.profile_put():
        self.storage_manager.batched_put(keys, memory_objs, ...)
except Exception as e:
    logger.error(
        "[req_id=%s] Store failed, releasing %d memory objects "
        "to prevent pin deadlock: %s", req_id, len(memory_objs), e,
    )
    for mo in memory_objs:
        try:
            if mo.is_pinned:
                mo.unpin()
            mo.ref_count_down()
        except Exception:
            pass
    return

Validation

Reproduced and validated the fix on 8x H200 with GLM-5-FP8:

Metric Before Fix After Fix
Allocation failures ~30 then hang 3,662+ (gracefully handled)
Pin timeouts (300s) 651 0
Server status Hung / unrecoverable Healthy (HTTP 200)
Disk cache growth 112 GB (stopped) 254 GB+ (still growing)

The stress test (lmcache_stress_test.py) with aggressive flooding (40 × 100K GPU + 200 × 50K CPU prompts) exhausted the 200 GB CPU tier. Before the fix, this caused the server to hang after ~3 hours of production traffic. After the fix, allocation failures are logged and skipped gracefully — zero pin timeouts, server remains responsive.

Note

The existing comment at cache_engine.py:1038-1039 already identified this class of bug on the retrieve path:

"Without this, pin_count stays at 1 forever and the CPU staging pool fills up, causing the next retrieve to deadlock inside allocate()."

The same pattern exists on the store and prefetch paths, which is what this fix addresses.

Discovered related bug: max_local_disk_size not enforced for MLA models

While running this branch in production with GLM-5-FP8 on H200, we observed /mnt/lmcache grow to 757 GB despite a configured max_local_disk_size: 500.0 cap — leading to a disk-full crash on our test server.

Root cause

The MLA multi-group fix correctly updates the read/write data path (raw_tensor, multi-group shapes/dtypes in DiskCacheMetadata), but the size accounting in local_disk_backend.py is not updated. The eviction policy still tracks size based on memory_obj.metadata.shape (singular, one group), while the actual file written to disk contains the full multi-group tensor.

Result: for every chunk LMCache thinks it stored X bytes, the file on disk is actually N×X bytes (where N is the number of groups). For GLM-5 MLA the ratio is ~1.5× — which matches our observed 757 GB / 500 GB = 1.51×.

Reproduction

  • Model: zai-org/GLM-5-FP8
  • Backend: local_disk only (with the patches in this PR applied)
  • Config: max_local_disk_size: 500.0, chunk_size: 256
  • After ~24h of production traffic: disk usage at 757 GB, eviction not firing

Fix in progress

We're preparing a follow-up patch to compute the chunk size from shapes/dtypes (plural) when present, so eviction tracks the actual on-disk footprint. Will add it to this PR shortly.

[Bugfix][MLA] Fix multi-group KV cache support for MLA models (GLM-5,…
fe55b79 
… DeepSeek V3)

Port of LMCache#2951. Fixes five crash/deadlock paths that
manifested on GLM-5-FP8 / DeepSeek V3 production deployments where the
KV cache is stored as two groups with different dtypes (K_rope uint8
head_dim=132 + latent KV bfloat16 head_dim=576).

Crash/leak fixes:
- memory_management.py: Raise ValueError on .tensor access for multi-group
  objects; use get_tensor(group_index) instead to prevent reshape crash.
- gpu_connectors.py: Fix _initialize_pointers() broadcast crash when
  actual_num_caches != num_layers; add per-group to_gpu/from_gpu transfer
  loops for multi-group memory objects using raw_tensor.
- cache_engine.py: Wrap store() from_gpu/batched_put in try/except with
  pin+ref cleanup on failure to prevent CPU staging pool exhaustion.
- local_disk_backend.py: Track pinned_disk_keys in batched_get_non_blocking
  and unpin all on allocation failure; fix disk accounting to use
  len(byte_array); clean up stale .pt leftovers on startup; propagate
  multi-group _shapes/_dtypes through disk round-trip.
- local_cpu_backend.py: Proportional eviction (target=max(2x,32MiB)) and
  MAX_ALLOC_ATTEMPTS=50 guard to prevent indefinite worker stall.

Also fixes save_only_first_rank lookup() to return total tokens for
non-first ranks (prevents min() aggregation zeroing).

Tests added:
- tests/v1/test_mla_multi_group.py: Unit tests for multi-group tensor
  access, raw_tensor, get_tensor(), and save_only_first_rank lookup.
- tests/v1/test_pin_lifecycle_invariants.py: 200-iteration random failure
  injection property test for pin/ref_count lifecycle invariants.
- Extended test_local_cpu_backend.py, test_local_disk_backend.py,
  test_address_manager.py, test_cache_engine.py with regression tests.

Validation update — blocker fixes confirmed working in production-like conditions

Both recent commits on this branch have been validated on 8x H200 running GLM-5.1-FP8 (zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8, TP=8, LMCache 0.4.2-g9d413181c, vLLM 0.19.0):

ef26de8 — LocalDiskBackend assert→None (#1918)

  • Bind-mounted onto a production-equivalent vLLM image
  • 800+ requests with 2 GiB CPU pool + 12-way concurrency
  • 0 crashes, 0 regressions, LMCache cache hits continued to serve correctly
  • The assert-trigger path itself wasn't reached during stress (the #1939 proportional-eviction fix keeps enough headroom that allocate() didn't return None under our workload). The change is strictly safer on the happy path regardless.

d62d903 — P2P allocator fmt from metadata.use_mla

  • Exercised with full P2P config: enable_p2p: true, enable_controller: true, 8 TP ranks registered with a sidecar controller, NIXL+UCX transfer channel
  • Critical log, all 8 TP workers: 
    Paged tensor memory allocator initialized,
  shapes: [torch.Size([1, 78, 256, 132]), torch.Size([1, 78, 256, 656])],
  dtypes: [torch.uint8, torch.uint8],
  align bytes: 15,734,784
    The 2-entry shapes list is definitive proof that KV_MLA_FMT was selected (a KV_2LTD init would produce a single-shape tensor). Confirms the metadata.use_mla-derived format is propagating end-to-end from config → LocalCPUBackend.initialize_allocator → PagedCpuGpuMemoryAllocator.
  • 5 inference requests with non-256-multiple token counts (197, 304, 636, 1160, 1736) exercised _get_unfull_chunk_shapes with self.fmt.token_dim(). All succeeded, zero AssertionError.

Notable config gotchas discovered during bring-up (not fixes to this PR, but worth knowing):

  • controller_pull_url/controller_reply_url must NOT include a tcp:// prefix — LMCache prepends it internally. A tcp://tcp://... double-prefix aborts init with Invalid argument (addr='tcp://tcp://...').
  • lmcache_worker_ids length must equal lmcache_worker_ports length. Defaulting lmcache_worker_ids=None silently becomes [0], which mismatches an 8-port list and fails an assertion-without-message during LMCacheWorker.__init__. A more informative error message (e.g., assert len(...) == len(...), "mismatched lengths") would save debugging time.

Taking this out of draft now that both patches are validated.

New commit: Wire LazyMemoryAllocator for single-process mode

Added e8387145 which replaces the LazyMixedMemoryAllocator is temporarily unavailable stub in local_cpu_backend.py with an actual LazyMemoryAllocator instantiation.

Problem

In single-process mode (our deployment), enable_lazy_memory_allocator: true was accepted but had no effect — the full CPU pool was always allocated upfront via a single cudaHostAlloc(size). This caused:

  1. cudaHostAlloc failed: 2 when max_local_cpu_size exceeds ~500 GB on H200 VMs — the CUDA driver or kernel can't handle a single pinned allocation that large (neuralwatt/inference_frontend#2764)
  2. CPU pool saturation — the full pool is allocated at boot, leaving no headroom for disk staging buffers. Under concurrent write traffic, all CPU entries get pinned for disk I/O, no eviction candidates remain, and new stores fail with 7k-63k "Failed to allocate memory block" warnings per server
  3. Cascading disk write failures — since the disk backend stages writes through the same CPU pool, CPU saturation blocks disk writes too, making the 1.5 TB disk pool unreachable

Fix

The LazyMemoryAllocator class already exists (PR #2407) and works in multi-process mode (distributed/memory_manager.py). This commit simply wires it into the single-process code path in local_cpu_backend.py:

if use_lazy:
    return LazyMemoryAllocator(
        init_size=cpu_size_bytes * config.lazy_memory_initial_ratio,
        final_size=cpu_size_bytes,
        align_bytes=align,
        numa_mapping=numa_mapping,
    )

With 64 MB pin chunks and 1 GB commit increments, no single cudaHostAlloc is large enough to hit the driver limit. The pool grows incrementally as traffic demands.

Production data (neuralwatt Kimi K2.6 + GLM-5.1 fleet)

Server Model Pin Timeouts Alloc Failures LMCache Version
rtp-14 GLM-5.1 0 29,482 wheel (0.4.4+nw)
rtp-01 GLM-5.1 1,461 63,835 bind-mount patches
h200-02 Kimi-K2.6 0 7,377 wheel (0.4.4+nw)
sweet-rain Kimi-K2.6 971 (stall) — bind-mount patches

The alloc failures directly impact end-user TTFT: failed stores mean cache misses on follow-up turns, forcing full cold prefill instead of APC hits.

Testing

Currently deploying the patched wheel to nebius-h200-test (Kimi K2.6, 8x H200) with max_local_cpu_size: 1000 (1 TB). Will report results.

fix(vllm_adapter): eager GPU connector init for MLA multi-group
910b83d 
`VLLMPagedMemGPUConnectorV3` lazily initializes its `KVLayerGroupsManager`
inside `from_gpu` / `to_gpu`. For MLA models whose physical KV cache splits
across multiple per-layer groups (e.g. GLM-5.1-FP8 has 2 groups: hs=132 and
hs=656), this lazy init happens AFTER `cache_engine.store` has already
allocated memory using the legacy single-group `kv_shape` from
`metadata.get_shapes()` (because `metadata.kv_layer_groups_manager` is still
`None` at that point).

The result: memory is sized for hs=576 (legacy `kv_shape[3]*kv_shape[4]`),
but `from_gpu` then iterates 2 groups and `lmc_ops.multi_layer_kv_transfer`
trips on the hidden-dim mismatch:

    Store failed during from_gpu/put: The size of tensor a (576) must
    match the size of tensor b (132) at non-singleton dimension 3

The pin-leak defensive cleanup branch fires and the request limps on
without storing anything, so the failure looks superficially like "cache
just isn't hitting" but in fact no store ever succeeds for fresh prompts
on these models.

The fix is to eagerly initialize the connector's layer-groups manager
during `register_kv_caches`, right after the kv_caches dict is captured.
This populates `metadata.kv_layer_groups_manager` before the first
`cache_engine.store` call, so `metadata.get_shapes()` returns the correct
per-group shapes and allocation matches what the connector expects.

The patch is gated by `hasattr` checks so non-V3 connectors (V2, SGLang,
layerwise) are unaffected — they don't have `_initialize_kv_cache_pointers`
and skip cleanly. The eager call is also re-entry safe via the existing
`if self.init: return` guard inside `_initialize_kv_cache_pointers`.

Reproduced and fixed against GLM-5.1-FP8 on H200 (TP=8, kv-cache-dtype=fp8).
Before: every fresh-prompt store fails with the shape mismatch above.
After: stores succeed at 10-15 GB/s, subsequent same-prompt requests hit
the LMCache lookup with `hit_tokens=1024`.

Refs: neuralwatt/inference_frontend#2746
Signed-off-by: Chad Gibson <ccgibson@hotmail.com>

Cross-class private method access _initialize_kv_cache_pointers

Low Severity

connector._initialize_kv_cache_pointers() accesses a private (_-prefixed) method of VLLMPagedMemGPUConnectorV3 from outside the class. Project conventions disallow cross-class private member access, and ruff SLF rules flag this pattern. Using only the public initialize_kvcaches_ptr (already called on line 743) or adding a public wrapper would respect the encapsulation boundary.

Bugbot Issues — Status Update

All 3 high-severity and the medium-severity issues have been addressed in the current branch. The bugbot reviews were against earlier commits.

Issue Status Details
HIGH: submit_put_task .tensor crash ✅ Fixed Line 349 uses raw_tensor, line 603 uses raw_tensor
HIGH: V2 to_gpu multi-group crash ✅ Fixed V2 to_gpu iterates per group with get_tensor(i) and per-group pointers

LOW: layout_hints missing ✅ Fixed Both to_gpu and from_gpu multi-group paths pass layout_hints=self.layout_hints

MED: Monkey-patching DiskCacheMetadata Deferred _shapes/_dtypes attrs work correctly; cleaner approach via dataclass fields can follow in #3106
MED: Eviction freed_bytes before removal False positive CPU entries always succeed removal; counting before is safe
LOW: evict_keys_count logging Cosmetic Not a correctness issue
LOW: Cross-class private method Won't fix Required for integration

Note on Gemma-4 (#3106)

The V2 connector's per-group head_size is correct for MLA models where all groups share the same page buffer geometry. For Gemma-4's asymmetric groups (different kv_heads × head_size per group), this will need updating — tracked in #3106 as part of the broader multi-group layout work.

ccgibson commented Apr 30, 2026

Copy link

Author

@jcbjoe Thanks for testing! The cudaErrorIllegalAddress during from_gpu store suggests a KV cache pointer/stride mismatch — most likely related to your TP configuration.

From your logs I can see:

  • GPU KV Cache Dimensions: [156][5127, 64, 132] — GLM-5.1-FP8 with MLA multi-group detected correctly
  • Only Worker_TP0 appears — are you running with --tensor-parallel-size 1?
  • 5127 blocks is higher than what we see at TP=8 (we get ~4171 blocks with --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85)

Our PR was validated at TP=8 only. With TP=1, the KV cache layout changes significantly — each rank holds all KV heads rather than a 1/8 shard, so the strides in multi_layer_kv_transfer are different. The _get_group_pointers pointer arithmetic may compute out-of-bounds offsets at TP=1, causing the illegal memory access.

Here are the vLLM arguments we use in production:

python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 \
    --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --tool-call-parser glm47 \
    --reasoning-parser glm45 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_buffer_size":4000000000}' \
    --enable-mfu-metrics \
    --chat-template-content-format=string \
    --structured-outputs-config '{"backend":"xgrammar","disable_any_whitespace":true}'

LMCache config:
chunk_size: 256
local_cpu: true
max_local_cpu_size: 500.0
local_disk: /mnt/lmcache
max_local_disk_size: 13000.0
save_decode_cache: false
enable_lazy_memory_allocator: true
lazy_memory_initial_ratio: 1.0
use_gpu_connector_v3: true

Key environment vars:
PYTHONHASHSEED=0
LMCACHE_CONFIG_FILE=/opt/lmcache/config.yaml

Image: vllm/vllm-openai:latest-cu130 (v0.19.x)

Could you confirm your --tensor-parallel-size and vLLM version?
If you're at TP=1, that's a configuration we haven't validated yet — the multi-group MLA pointer arithmetic assumes the TP-sharded KV head layout. I can look into adding TP=1 support if that's the case.

Hey @jcbjoe, glad it's working for you! Re: CacheBlend — that's a separate feature from this PR's scope (multi-group MLA storage). Our PR fixes the underlying KV format issue but doesn't extend the blending code path to handle MLA's per-group recompute. We haven't tested enable_blending: true on MLA models with these patches, so I can't say it works correctly today. Adding proper MLA support to CacheBlend's layer-recompute path would be a follow-up PR — happy to discuss the design if you or your team want to take a swing at it. We're focused on getting this PR merged for production use first.

@biondizzle — appreciate you tracking this down and sharing the patch. We've been chasing the same crash and it lines up with vllm-project/vllm#40989 (still open upstream), which is the same context_lens.is_contiguous() fix you applied.

One thing that might save you some pain later: in our own testing on vLLM v0.20.x + spec decode, we also hit a separate hang under sustained traffic — multiproc_executor.collective_rpc() deadline staleness causing sample_tokens RPC to time out with EngineDeadError after typically 7-15 min. We filed that as vllm-project/vllm#40926 and the fix is vllm-project/vllm#41357 (also still open).

@kabletv ran a canary in this thread combining both PRs (#40989 + #41357) on GLM-5.1-FP8 + MTP=3 and got a clean 30-min soak. We haven't done a multi-hour soak ourselves yet so can't promise it's bulletproof, but that combination is what we're planning to deploy when we re-attempt MTP. Sharing in case it helps you avoid debugging the same thing twice.

The only thing is, I occasionally see this error in the vllm logs:

    (Worker_TP2 pid=767) [2026-05-06 15:56:03,745] LMCache ERROR: Request chatcmpl-3fb08ae0-a0cc-4f52-86e0-de85aeee8f3c-83f6e6b1The number of retrieved tokens is less than the expected number of tokens! This should not happen! (vllm_v1_adapter.py:878:lmcache.integration.vllm.vllm_v1_adapter)
(Worker_TP2 pid=767) [2026-05-06 15:56:03,745] LMCache ERROR: Num retrieved tokens: 49664, num expected tokens: 55808 (vllm_v1_adapter.py:884:lmcache.integration.vllm.vllm_v1_adapter)

I think it's because i have this set in the config: https://sweetapi.com/biondizzle/vllm-with-lmcache/src/branch/dream-build-glm/lmcache-config-glm-51.yaml#L4

So maybe that's making it not save the spec decode tokens. Im going to try out setting that to true and seeing if that error goes away

EDIT:
YEP That fixed it. Setting save_decode_cache: true made it so the spec decode tokens get stored in cache and we no longer get that error

EDIT 1 DAY Later:
It did not fix the issue. Still see quite a few of these in the logs:

(Worker_TP0 pid=628) [2026-05-07 14:45:02,928] LMCache ERROR: Request chatcmpl-efba0bef-abd2-4d0f-bc4e-7e6b3c59253e-8288da24The number of retrieved tokens is less than the expected number of tokens! This should not happen! (vllm_v1_adapter.py:878:lmcache.integration.vllm.vllm_v1_adapter)
(Worker_TP0 pid=628) [2026-05-07 14:45:02,928] LMCache ERROR: Num retrieved tokens: 1280, num expected tokens: 15616 (vllm_v1_adapter.py:884:lmcache.integration.vllm.vllm_v1_adapter)

I'm thinking my build didn't have #3189 and that error is coming from the local system ram cache as opposed to the offload cache.
